channel.title: Crypto Asia news
channel.description: Short crypto news briefs with links to the original publishers.

item.title: Kazakhstan to issue tokenized government bonds next quarter
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to launch tokenized government bonds in the first quarter, following its first sale of tokenized central bank notes. The move comes as the country expands its crypto market. (Source: CoinDesk)

item.title: UK, Singapore and Thailand central banks test cross-border FX settlement
item.description: A project called Meridian FX APAC showed how transactions can be coordinated between traditional settlement systems and blockchain-based ones. The test involves central banks from the UK, Singapore and Thailand. (Source: CoinDesk)

item.title: HYPE Token Holds Up Better Than Bitcoin and Ether in Selloff
item.description: Hyperliquid's HYPE token has fallen about a quarter from its peak but is outperforming Bitcoin and Ethereum during the latest market downturn. Its derivatives market is cited as one possible reason, with HYPE near $73 on Friday. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Market makers may be amplifying bitcoin and ether price swings
item.description: Bitcoin and ether are trading in ranges where market makers and dealers could be adding to volatility. The excerpt is brief and offers no further detail. (Source: CoinDesk)

item.title: AAVE Drops 30% Over Four Weeks, Worse Than BTC and ETH
item.description: The Aave governance token fell further than bitcoin and ether over the period, while the dollar value of assets locked on Aave declined by a smaller percentage. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Unocoin pauses all services after hackers get around BitGo freeze
item.description: Indian exchange Unocoin says disputed transfers were signed outside BitGo while it investigates suspected misuse of a backup mechanism. The firm has halted all services during the probe. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Glassnode Data Flags Quantum Risk for Over a Third of Bitcoin
item.description: Analytics firm Glassnode counted about 7.12 million bitcoin whose public keys already appear on the public ledger, a potential quantum vulnerability. Most owners could fix it quickly, but some early coins may never be secured. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Grayscale Says Crypto Offers Opportunities Beyond Bitcoin
item.description: Grayscale said crypto's growth is opening investment options beyond bitcoin, as sectors differ in business models, adoption and token economics. Its analysis links weakening correlations to a greater role for picking individual assets, while noting marketwide risks remain. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: BitGo rejects breach claims as Unocoin investigates transfers
item.description: BitGo says the disputed transfers were made with keys held by Unocoin and without its involvement. Unocoin suspects a backup mechanism was misused, and its services remain suspended. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Trump Names First Democrats for SEC and CFTC Posts
item.description: Trump has proposed a bipartisan slate of two Republicans and two Democrats for the SEC and CFTC, his first Democratic picks for either agency. The nominees would fill commissions that shape crypto policy. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: Bitcoin slides to 12-week low as rate-hike worries erase rally
item.description: Bitcoin has fallen back to around August price levels as stubborn inflation, rising expectations of another rate increase and ETF outflows weigh on the market. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: About $600M in Long Positions Liquidated as Bitcoin, Ether Drop
item.description: Traders betting on higher prices lost $599 million in 24 hours as Bitcoin and Ethereum fell to their lowest levels in nearly three months. Longs accounted for 88% of $680.81 million in total crypto liquidations. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Bitcoin Falls to Around $70,600 Amid Extended Losses
item.description: Bitcoin slid to about $70,600 as its four-week decline deepened. Coinbase also hit a fresh 28-day low, and ether kept trailing bitcoin over one- and four-week periods. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Visa to Settle Stablecoin Transactions Using Western Union's USDPT
item.description: Anchorage Digital is working with Visa so that certain stablecoins issued by its federally regulated bank, beginning with Western Union's USDPT, can serve as settlement assets on Visanet. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Aave user loses $305,000 in Across Protocol website hijack
item.description: A user reportedly lost about $305,000 from an Aave deposit token after the Across Protocol website was hijacked. Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery estimates total losses of roughly $401,900 across nine wallets. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Binance says hacked assets are covered; proof pending
item.description: Binance says it has closed the remaining gap in customer backing. Users will need to wait for cryptographic proof of a new snapshot before they can verify it. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Sky advisor suggests pausing new borrowing from core vaults
item.description: BA Labs, a Sky advisor, has proposed stopping new borrowing from core vaults, which would leave existing borrowers able to repay and manage collateral but not mint more. The report cites 771 open vaults holding about 376.33 million USDS in debt. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: New York regulator sets 2027 deadline for crypto marketing rules
item.description: New York's financial regulator will require BitLicense holders and crypto trust companies to prepare annually approved marketing policies. The policies are to cover risk disclosures, paid promoters and misleading claims, with a May 2027 deadline. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: New York regulator issues crypto advertising guidance for firms
item.description: The New York Department of Financial Services has released guidance setting out what it expects crypto firms to do when creating policies and procedures for advertising and marketing. (Source: The Block)

item.title: DOJ, Banks and DeFi Groups Back Suit Against Illinois Crypto Tax
item.description: The Justice Department, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, SIFMA and a crypto coalition including a16z, Paradigm and Uniswap have filed briefs supporting a lawsuit seeking to invalidate Illinois' 0.2% tax on digital asset transactions. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: Crypto industry says Illinois crypto tax can't be enforced as written
item.description: Crypto industry groups have filed opposition in a court challenge to a crypto transaction tax in Illinois, arguing the tax would not work in practice. (Source: CoinDesk)

item.title: Bitcoin dominance tests 61% level; altcoin impact discussed
item.description: Bitcoin's market dominance is testing a 61% breakout level, and a weekly Supertrend indicator has flipped bullish. The piece looks at what this could mean for altcoins. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Solana Company posts Q3 revenue rise on staking rewards
item.description: Solana Company, a digital asset treasury firm, reported quarterly revenue of $3.4 million, up from $697,000 a year earlier. The company's growth was linked to staking rewards. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Large Bitcoin holders accumulate as ETF investors pull out funds
item.description: Glassnode data through November 9 shows a narrow pattern of whale accumulation, while Bitcoin ETF sessions through November 10 still recorded outflows. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Zcash Slides Under $965 After 26% Weekly Drop
item.description: Zcash's seven-day decline was about three times larger than bitcoin's. The token now trades roughly 43% below its late-September level. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Bitcoin Heads for First Back-to-Back Annual Losses
item.description: Bitcoin is on track for two consecutive years of losses, which would break a long-running pattern of annual gains. The excerpt notes that the data contains some nuance. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: Bitcoin Recovers Above $74,000 Following Inflation-Driven Dip
item.description: Bitcoin climbed back above $74,600 after falling to $72,787 when U.S. inflation data came in hotter than expected. Market-wide liquidations totaled $199 million, with $51 million tied to bitcoin. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Stablecoin supply shrinks by $14.2 billion, largest drop since 2022
item.description: Total stablecoin supply fell by $14.2 billion, the steepest contraction since the 2022 downturn. USDT and USDC together dropped by nearly $11 billion over the past month, while gold-backed tokens stayed flat. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Helius Unveils Privacy Rings Protocol for Solana Transactions
item.description: Solana Privacy Rings are a protocol from Helius that encrypt balances and transfer amounts while keeping activity on the Solana network. The piece explains how the system works and how it compares to alternatives. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: LlamaRisk Suggests Borrow Rate Limits for Aave V3
item.description: Risk firm LlamaRisk has proposed timed borrowing buffers for Aave V3, alongside a steward-managed route for large clients. The parameters are still provisional, and governance votes have not yet taken place. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Apex Group joins Hedera Council, eyeing tokenization and settlement
item.description: Apex Group, which oversees $3.5 trillion in assets, has joined the Hedera Council. It plans to explore Hedera for tokenization, compliance and settlement. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Bitcoin Core patches high-severity bug that could halt mining
item.description: Bitcoin Core developers have fixed three bugs, including a serious one that could stop miners from building new blocks. The flaws involve denial-of-service and privacy issues rather than theft of coins. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: Pyth Network brings NYSE stock and ETF data to marketplace
item.description: Pyth Network has added real-time stock and ETF data from the New York Stock Exchange to its data marketplace. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Bitcoin steadies near $74K as stocks gain amid yield rise
item.description: Bitcoin moved within a tight band while investors bought dips in tech shares. Meanwhile, US bond yields rose after inflation data came in high. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: StoneX keeps Buy rating on Securitize, citing tokenization growth
item.description: StoneX reaffirmed its Buy recommendation on Securitize, pointing to tokenized equities, fund demand and structured credit as drivers of growth. The brief is based on a short excerpt, so further details are not covered here. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Solana perpetuals volume jumps 65% as spot trading shrinks
item.description: Perpetual futures trading on Solana has surged, with one venue making up about 77% of weekly turnover in DefiLlama's Solana data. The growth comes as stablecoin market capitalization declines. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: LNbits issues urgent patch following reported Bitcoin wallet thefts
item.description: The LNbits project warned that installations on older versions are vulnerable and advised operators to replace potentially exposed credentials even after upgrading. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: Former Ripple CTO says no hidden XRP plan exists
item.description: David Schwartz, Ripple's CTO Emeritus, told frustrated XRP holders that the token's price mostly tracks the broader market. He said there is no secret plan behind XRP. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Ether Dips Near $2,000 as Stakers Hold Firm
item.description: Ether briefly fell toward $2,000 after hotter-than-expected US inflation data unsettled markets, then recovered to around $2,060. Staking data shows investors showing little interest in withdrawing their staked ETH. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Major Banks Put $270M Behind Stablecoin Issuer Project
item.description: Goldman Sachs, Citi and other global banks have committed $270 million to a U.S.-incorporated stablecoin issuer codenamed Project Faro. The funding covers five years of operations as traditional lenders seek to compete with Tether and Circle. (Source: Decrypt)
